We need answer how are two range-level seeding assignments related within one retained EU. Evidence: "Within an EU, seeding is randomly assigned to one range and not the other. The authors explicitly say the Medicine Bow assignment plot would have the opposite shading from the Sierra Madre plot." This suggests one joint allocation selects seeded range, other complementary unseeded. Options: independent_assignments: each range independently randomized, both/neither can be seeded. complementary_assignment: One joint allocation selects seeded range, other receives complementary unseeded. both_seeded: both ranges assigned seeding together as one treated pair. permanent_range: one range permanently assigned seeding and other remains unseeded throughout. other/not_stated/conflicting.

Evidence clearly: seeding randomly assigned to one range and not the other within EU. Opposite shading. So complementary_assignment. q1 = complementary_assignment.

q2: Does an assigned-unseeded label, by itself, establish zero physical exposure to seeding material? Evidence: scope says "auxiliary gauges and possible cross-range contamination do not redefine the assigned treatment." Also CLOUD-2014 slides: ground-based ice-nucleus measurements indicating silver iodide reached Medicine Bow in 21 Sierra Madre seeding cases; 18 modeled cases enhanced precipitation in Medicine Bow during Sierra Madre seeding. This implies unseeded range (Medicine Bow when Sierra Madre seeded) may be physically exposed due to cross-range contamination. So assigned-unseeded label does not establish zero physical exposure; it's assignment only. Option assignment_only: "No; it establishes the planned allocation, while physical exposure requires additional evidence because cross-range contamination is discussed." That fits. q2 = assignment_only.
